claims.title: The price of a mixed jet
claims.statement: For the finite multi-index κ≤a coordinatewise and the ultrametric field, integral series, root-of-unity invariance, row weights and substitutions specified in the chapter, the factored jet has normalized valuation at least ∑κᵢ(γₚ−σᵢ)−|ι|(logₚ a+1). Each offending pure pair below κ requires p^ασᵢ+p^βσⱼ≥1.
claims.correspondence: The proof raises the radii, bounds the integral substitution and exponential separately, then multiplies by the multifactorial. The full BHyp realization is open in this exposition.

claims.title: Feasible row corrections
claims.statement: For an odd prime and an even cycle of at least two row labels, assume the coefficient, integrality, cancellation and row-capacity conditions of the mixed-jet estimate. The corrections σᵢ can be chosen within the row budgets so that p^ασᵢ+p^βσⱼ≥1 for every offending pair. These corrections give the stated valuation bound for each admissible derivative.
claims.correspondence: The local-mixed section identifies the optimizer inputs and constraints. The local-radii section derives the dual optimum, its cyclic row assembly and its use in the monomial coefficient bound. Applying the result to all global host data still requires additional arithmetic input.

claims.title: Transport of the normalized theta vector
claims.statement: Fix the CM curve ideal, its nonzero twelfth-root normalization, an admissible character and two admitted lattices. A complex linear isometry identifying their period lattices and Hermitian forms carries the normalized theta vector to a holomorphic function on the target with its signed translation law, provided the two discriminant parameters agree.
claims.correspondence: Holomorphicity is pulled back along a complex linear equivalence; rational integrality converts its translation phase to (−1)^m.

claims.title: Passing to every level
claims.statement: For N>0, Re s>½ and (χ≠1 or s≠1), nonvanishing for the inducing primitive character gives L(χ,s)≠0. At positive real part each extra factor is nonzero because |ψ(p)p^(−s)|≤p^(−Re s)<1.

claims.title: Reflection of a character zero
claims.statement: For a primitive ψ of nonzero modulus and a zero with 0<Re s<1, L(ψ⁻¹,1−s)=0. For arbitrary χ the primitive transfer and right-half-plane nonvanishing imply Re s=½.

claims.title: Classical reflection with the exceptional integers
claims.statement: If ζ(s)≠0 for Re s>½ and s≠1, every zero away from 1 and the negative even integers has real part ½.
